hooks.command: input=$(cat); cmd=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty'); if echo "$cmd" | grep -qE '^git (checkout -b|switch -c)'; then current=$(git -C $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null); if [ "$current" != "main" ]; then printf '{"continue":false,"stopReason":"Branch rule: new branches must be created from main. Currently on: %s. Run: git checkout main first."}' "$current"; exit 0; fi; fi

hooks.prompt:
You are a skill-gap detector for Petrobrain (DCS World Model Builder), running right after the dod (Definition of Done) agent finished. Review the tool calls made in this session. Count how many times each distinct action pattern was repeated (e.g., same Bash command structure, same type of file edit, same Read pattern on similar paths). Before flagging anything, establish what this project ALREADY has, by running:
  ls $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/
  grep -h '^description:' $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/*.md $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md
Every `<name>.md` there is a user-invocable slash command `/<name>`; every subdirectory is a skill. CRUCIAL: the `.md` slash commands are invoked by the user typing `/<name>`, so they NEVER appear as `Skill`-tool calls in the transcript. The absence of a `Skill` invocation is therefore NOT evidence that the capability is missing. If an existing command or skill already covers a repeated pattern, do not flag it.

If any action type was done 3 or more times AND no existing skill or slash command covers it, append a candidate entry to $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/agent-memory/skill-candidates.md using this format:

## <YYYY-MM-DD> <short-pattern-name>
- **Pattern**: <concise description of what was done repeatedly>
- **Count**: N times this session
- **Benefit**: <why a reusable skill would help future agents>

Only add entries for patterns not already present in the file — including its "Resolved" section, which records patterns already created or already rejected with reasons; never re-flag one of those. Only flag clear, repeated, automatable patterns — not one-off actions, not things already covered by an existing skill or slash command, and not generic file I/O that a built-in tool already does (reading line ranges is the Read tool's offset/limit; read-transform-write of a file is the Edit tool). Such patterns look repetitive only because of how this session's tools happened to be configured. If nothing qualifies, do nothing and exit silently.
